ledger.sentence: A colonoscopy is often done to look for the cause of bowel symptoms, such as abdominal pain or a change in bowel habit.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US source) says doctors order colonoscopy for symptoms such as abdominal pain, changes in bowel movements or weight loss. The NHS wording was not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Colonoscopy is also used to follow up after earlier polyps or bowel cancer, according to MedlinePlus, a US source.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US) lists follow-up of earlier polyps or colon cancer. 'Early signs in people at high risk' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: People who have had polyps removed before are routinely advised to have repeat colonoscopies.
ledger.note: Retrieved PMC text: repeat colonoscopy is routinely recommended after polyp removal; family history at least doubles risk. No text on referral for family history.

ledger.sentence: For a clear view, the bowel needs to be empty.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: the colon must be emptied first because problems may be missed if the intestines are not cleaned out (US source).

ledger.sentence: Preparation can include laxatives to empty the bowel.
ledger.note: Laxatives are mentioned (MedlinePlus, US) but 'trusts generally' and 'powder mixed with water' were not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Preparation can include clear liquids the day before and laxatives, according to MedlinePlus, a US source.
ledger.note: Not retrieved for a specific trust. MedlinePlus (US) says prep can include enemas, clear liquids the day before and laxatives.

ledger.sentence: A review of bowel preparation lists vomiting, colicky stomach ache and dizziness among the most common problems.
ledger.note: A review (PMC) lists vomiting, colicky stomach ache and dizziness among the most common prep problems; diarrhoea and 'stay near a toilet' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Preparation depends on which type the doctor recommends, and it can differ between hospitals.
ledger.note: Only partly: MedlinePlus says the type of prep depends on what the doctor recommends. 'Hospital sends own instructions' not retrieved verbatim.

ledger.sentence: A nurse sees the person first to discuss their medical history, carry out simple checks and explain what will happen.
ledger.note: NHS pages: a nurse checks details, explains the procedure and risks, and checks pulse, blood pressure and oxygen levels.

ledger.sentence: A thin, flexible tube with a camera is passed through the anus and around the large bowel.
ledger.note: NHS pages: a thin, flexible tube with a camera goes in through the anus.

ledger.sentence: Air is pumped in to open the bowel, which can cause bloating or cramps.
ledger.note: NHS pages: air or gas is passed through the tube to open the bowel; can cause bloating and cramping.

ledger.sentence: The NHS says a colonoscopy can be uncomfortable but should not be painful.
ledger.note: NHS says the camera may be felt going in but it should not hurt; cramping is common. One trust leaflet warns it can sometimes be quite painful.

ledger.sentence: NHS England says a colonoscopy should take 30 to 45 minutes, and a person may be at the hospital for around two hours in total.
ledger.note: NHS England says it should take 30 to 45 minutes and you might be at the hospital for around 2 hours. Other trusts quote different times; unattributed sentence should name the source.

ledger.sentence: A leaflet says some people have sedation, some breathe a pain-relieving gas called Entonox, and some have no pain relief.
ledger.note: Trust pages: choice of sedation, Entonox (gas and air) or neither.

ledger.sentence: Sedation is given through a thin tube called a cannula in the hand or arm.
ledger.note: Sources say sedation goes through a cannula in the hand or arm; 'needle in back of hand' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Polyps are growths on the bowel lining, and they are usually not cancer.
ledger.note: PMC text: most polyps are benign; hyperplastic polyps carry no cancer risk, adenomas can progress.

ledger.sentence: Doctors usually cannot tell the type of polyp just by looking, so suspicious polyps are usually removed and examined under a microscope.
ledger.note: PMC text: the physician usually cannot tell polyp type by eye, so suspicious polyps are usually removed and sent for microscope examination. 'Not possible' is stronger than retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Staff can also take small tissue samples, called biopsies, which people typically do not feel.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US) and trusts: tissue samples are taken with forceps or snare and patients typically do not feel it.

ledger.sentence: Some findings may be shared once the sedation has worn off, according to MedlinePlus, a US source.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US): some findings are shared after sedation wears off; 'usually told whether polyps removed' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: NHS trust leaflets describe colonoscopy as very safe, with serious complications rare.
ledger.note: Not retrieved as an NHS statement. Trust leaflets describe colonoscopy as very safe with serious complications rare.

ledger.sentence: The main risks are a tear in the bowel wall, called perforation, and bleeding.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US) and trust leaflets: bleeding and perforation are the main complications.

ledger.sentence: Trust leaflets give perforation figures that differ, and one says about 1 in 1,000 procedures.
ledger.note: Trust leaflets give about 1 in 1,500, less than 1 in 1,700 and about 1 in 1,000 procedures. 'Nationally' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The risk rises when polyps are removed, especially large or complex ones.
ledger.note: Trust leaflets: polyp removal raises bleeding and perforation risk; one gives 1 in 500 to 1 in 20 depending on polyp size, location and difficulty.

ledger.sentence: A perforation is treated in hospital, and surgery is sometimes needed, according to NHS trust leaflets.
ledger.note: Clip closure not retrieved. Leaflets say repair often needs surgery; one says antibiotics and rest can sometimes settle it.

ledger.sentence: It is common to pass a small amount of blood from the anus after a biopsy or polyp removal.
ledger.note: Trust leaflets: small amounts of blood are expected after biopsy or polyp removal; North Tees says it can occur up to 2 weeks later.

ledger.sentence: Trust leaflets say a colonoscopy can occasionally miss a problem, including, rarely, a cancer.
ledger.note: Frimley leaflet: chance of missing cancer or a polyp approx 3 in 100; other trusts say occasional, rarely cancer. 'Very accurate' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The NHS says to call NHS 111 or the hospital where the test was done for some symptoms after a colonoscopy, and to call 999 or go to A&E for more serious ones; its page lists which symptoms apply.
ledger.note: NHS colonoscopy page: call 111 or the hospital for some symptoms, 999 or A&E for more serious ones; full symptom list not retrieved, so specific symptoms (fever, heavy bleeding) not confirmed.

ledger.sentence: Some NHS trusts say a letter or call with the results comes about two to three weeks after a colonoscopy, though waits can differ.
ledger.note: NHS trust pages: letter or call about 2 to 3 weeks after; other trusts quote longer waits for biopsy results.

ledger.sentence: The result will say whether anything abnormal was found and whether further treatment is needed, according to NHS trust pages.
ledger.note: Not retrieved. Sources say the results say whether things are normal or need treatment; a normal result does not exclude a missed finding (leaflets note missed problems).

ledger.sentence: If a biopsy was taken, trust leaflets give differing waits for the biopsy results, from several days to several weeks.
ledger.note: Retrieved waits for biopsy/polyp results: several days, usually within 2-3 weeks, 4-6 weeks, 8-10 weeks. 'Up to two weeks' not supported.

ledger.sentence: A colonoscopy passes a thin, flexible tube with a camera through the bowel to look for the cause of symptoms, to screen for bowel cancer, or to follow up earlier problems.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus (US): symptoms and follow-up of polyps/cancer; screening shown by NHS England bowel screening guide and Frimley 'Bowel Cancer Screening' colonoscopy leaflet (titles/snippets).

ledger.sentence: The bowel must be empty for a clear view, so a bowel preparation, which can include laxatives, is taken beforehand.
ledger.note: Empty bowel supported (MedlinePlus, US); 'often causes frequent diarrhoea' not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Polyps, which are growths on the bowel lining, can be removed during the test and examined under a microscope.
ledger.note: Polyps are removed (snare/forceps) and suspicious ones examined under a microscope (PMC; MedlinePlus).

ledger.sentence: Perforation, a tear in the bowel wall, is the main serious risk and is uncommon, with higher risk when polyps are removed.
ledger.note: Trust leaflets: bleeding and perforation are the main risks, serious complications rare; polyp removal raises risk.
